claim: Every one of the eleven file sizes on the Qwen3.8-35B-A3B GGUF card is exact. All eleven round-trip to the byte at three decimal places, the card states its unit convention out loud (1 GB = 1,000,000,000 bytes), and a vision projector now ships alongside the text quants. That is a direct fix of the failure this article opened with: the 2B release was sold on '~1 GB on a phone' against a smallest file of 1.312 GB.
method: curl -sSL -I against huggingface.co for every file in empero-ai/Qwen3.8-35B-A3B-Distill-GGUF, reading Content-Length after the CDN redirect rather than the git-lfs pointer. Parameter counts come from HTTP range reads of the 21 safetensors shard headers plus model-mtp.safetensors in empero-ai/Qwen3.8-35B-A3B-Distill — the 8-byte length prefix, then the JSON header — with each tensor's shape multiplied out; no weight bytes were downloaded.
note: Parameter accounting, measured the same way: 35,951,822,704 total across all 22 safetensors files, every tensor BF16. That splits into model.language_model 34,152,051,328 + lm_head 508,559,360 (= the card's '34.7B text path'), model.visual 446,571,248, and an mtp block of 844,640,768 in its own file. Active per token — dense body 1,813,885,568, shared experts 125,911,040, and 8/256 of 32,212,254,720 routed-expert parameters — is 2,946,429,568, so 'A3B' is honest. model.safetensors.index.json is not: its total_size (71,903,645,408) counts the MTP file's bytes while its total_parameters (35,107,181,936) excludes the MTP file's parameters, which is why the Hugging Face API prints a BF16 parameter count larger than the total.
